identity.fantasy: A glyphic elementalist who writes Frost, Flame, and Arcane effects in sequence, then releases them through Glyphic Ruin and larger manuscript windows.
identity.one_line: A Glyph builder/spender. Elemental spells grant Frost, Flame, and Arcane Glyphs; Glyphic Ruin unleashes the active effect; Overload, Manuscription, and Chapters create larger multi-school sequences. It has flexible control and AoE, but the correct order of attunements and Glyph releases matters.

mechanics.core_loop: Choose tattoos and weapon runes before combat, generate the required glyph count with Elemental Blast and Primordial Blast, consume it with Glyphic Ruin or Thaumaturgy, keep Primordial Pulse moving, and empty charges before Runic Obliteration rebuilds and resets the sequence.

modes.name: Runic Obliteration
modes.structural_description: Level 50 PassiveUsing Elemental Burst now has a 20% chance to transform your next Primordial Blast into Runic Obliteration for 10 seconds.Runic Obliteration (Spell)Hurl powerful elemental missiles at an enemy, dealing 250 + 44% SP Elemental Damage every 0 sec for 1 seconds. Each missile grants you a Glyph.Scales with modifiers to Primordial Blast.

mechanics.single_target: The documented build generates two glyphs, prioritizes Glyphic Ruin during Zenith, extends proc-based Frigid Blast near expiry, and avoids hard-casting it outside the Warpdagger setup.
mechanics.aoe: The AoE sequence generates and consumes three glyphs, uses Primordial Pulse on cooldown, and groups Zenith, Glyphic Overload, and Manuscription into a repeatable burst window.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: Runeshroud, Phase Out, Warpdagger macros, and cursor runes support repositioning, but the ordered glyph sequence still rewards planned casts.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Glacial, Silencing, resonance, invisibility, and leyline tools provide broad caster control; the captured build deliberately chooses offense over defense.
mechanics.group_utility: Control runes, dispel support, interrupts, and threat redirection add utility around the damage cycle.

failure_modes.text: Consuming the wrong glyph count, using Runic Obliteration before emptying charges, or entering the burst macro with the wrong tattoo and rune setup wastes resets and elemental releases.

Movement or a target swap can interrupt the intended payoff: runeshroud, phase out, warpdagger macros, and cursor runes support repositioning, but the ordered glyph sequence still rewards planned casts.

Spending recovery or control too early leaves less protection for the next pressure event: glacial, silencing, resonance, invisibility, and leyline tools provide broad caster control; the captured build deliberately chooses offense over defense.

claims.text: The July Glyphic guide documents separate AoE and single-target sequences, pre-pull tattoo and weapon-rune choices, Warpdagger buff macros, two-glyph versus three-glyph consumption, Zenith priority, Primordial Pulse resets, Frigid Blast proc extension, and emptying charges before Runic Obliteration. It explicitly covers PvE rather than PvP.
claims.notes: The source is Portuguese; mechanics were normalized without copying its prose.

claims.text: Recent Runemaster discussion describes high APM and survivability pressure, while also reporting that the Glyphic version changes materially and feels stronger once level-50 tools arrive.
claims.notes: Community naming Glyphic maps to current dataset name Arcane.

claims.text: The July DPS compilation reports Glyphic at 3,993, and the August Mythic inventory lists 79 Arcane or Glyphic records.
claims.notes: Arcane is the dataset label; Glyphic is the community label. Sources are unnormalized.

claims.text: Arcane Runemaster's difficulty comes from preserving an ordered state machine rather than merely pressing many spells: glyph counts, releases, resets, tattoos, and burst windows can invalidate one another when sequenced poorly.
claims.notes: Playstyle classification from the documented rotations.
